newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco stocks close higher, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Morocco stocks close higher, led by banks.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.84 percent higher, helped by the banking sector, while ONA group lost ground, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 467.41 points from 463.50 points on Wednesday.
"We can note that ONA group is losing ground together with Samir oil refinery, while the banking sector is climbing," Magid Benjelloun, analyst at Maroc Inter Titres, said.
ONA group shed one dirham to close at 590 dirhams.
But ONA group subsidiaries, edible oil firm Lesieur Uni and sugar company Cosumar, jumped respectively 51 dirhams to 1400 dirhams and 10 dirhams to 790 dirhams.
Morocco's second largest conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement was up five dirhams to close at 565 dirhams.
Wafabank, a liquid stock which recently merged with Spanish Uniban bank, gained five dirhams to 570 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur was up 10 dirhams to 430 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie rose 10 dirhams to close at 341 dirhams.
Credit firm Eqdom Credit, which said on Thursday it had increased its capital by more than 50.3 percent to 167.02 million dirhams ($18.9 million), was up 25 dirhams to close at 857 dirhams.
Brewery firm, Brasseries du Maroc, gained 23 dirhams to close at 1550 dirhams.
Samir refinery shed two dirhams to close at 238 dirhams.
Morocco planned to sell 31 to 51 percent of Samir to foreign investors before December 1996. It had floated 25 percent of its stake early last year.
"It was a strategic mistake to privatise Samir refinery, we do not sell a company which has no hard core of shareholders," Benjelloum said.
Traded volume on the official market was 43.6 million dirhams, down from 50.8 million on Wednesday.
